title: Cross-compilation and a single binary in a distroless container

videos.script: boxoffice is about to leave your machine. It goes as one file, inside an image with almost nothing else in it. {{engine}} First a container engine: Docker Engine on Ubuntu, and what to do when the first command is refused. {{cross}} Then the Go toolchain builds for Linux, macOS and Windows, on Intel and on ARM, from one machine, with two variables. {{static}} One of those builds turns out dynamically linked. Turning cgo off makes it a single static file, and three flags make it a release that knows its own version. {{image}} The image is distroless: no shell, no package manager, seven megabytes to download. The dynamic binary fails inside it, with a message about a file that is plainly there. {{run}} Running it needs everything handed in from outside: a port, the database socket, a user, a token file. Lesson fourteen's configuration does the work. {{arm}} Last, an image for ARM servers, built without emulating anything, because Go already compiled for them.
